title: Role of Resonant $\mathbf{k}$-Points in the Transient Optical Response of Pumped Germanium
authors: Amir Eskandari-asl, Giacomo Inzani, Matteo Lucchini, Adolfo Avella
abstract: Pump-induced transient optical properties combine contributions from electronic states throughout the Brillouin zone, but the relative relevance of off-resonant and l-photon resonant crystal momenta has remained unexplored. We address this issue in pumped germanium by resolving the transient absorptive response into momentum-space classes defined by the presence or absence of 1-, 2-, and 3-photon resonances with respect to the pump. Using the Dynamical Projective Operatorial Approach together with the related generalized linear response theory, we compute the differential imaginary part of the dielectric function and evaluate the contributions of each resonance class. Resonant regions account for nearly the entire optical response, whereas points outside the identified resonance sets contribute only negligibly. Nevertheless, the 2-photon-resonant set, although containing more than 98% of the residual (post-pump) excitation population, does not reproduce the full transient spectrum. Conversely, resonance classes with very small residual populations generate non-negligible contributions to the transient optical properties. This mismatch shows that the transient optical weight is not determined solely by the real-charge dynamics (which results in post-pulse residual excitation population) and is consistent with substantial virtual pump-induced contributions, whose dominant optical weight nevertheless arises from the resonant regions of momentum space. The class-resolved phase of the dominant 2$ω_{\mathrm{pu}}$ oscillations further shows that, whenever a class contributes appreciably, the phase of its oscillatory component follows that of the corresponding full signal. The resulting decomposition provides a momentum-resolved connection among multi-photon resonances and transient optical observables in a realistic material.
summary: The paper investigates the transient optical response of pumped Germanium by decomposing it based on multi-photon resonance conditions across the Brillouin zone. Using advanced linear response theory, the authors show that while most excited carriers reside at 2-photon resonant points, the full optical signal requires contributions from virtual processes beyond just these real-charge excitations. This establishes a powerful momentum-resolved connection between pump resonances and ultrafast optical observables.
main_problem: The study aims to resolve the momentum-space origin of transient optical response in pumped Germanium by determining the relative importance of off-resonant versus $l$-photon resonant crystal momenta.
main_result: The transient optical weight is not solely determined by real-charge dynamics (residual population) but requires substantial virtual pump-induced contributions, although the dominant weight still arises from resonant momentum regions.
method: The authors use a Dynamical Projective Operatorial Approach combined with generalized linear response theory to decompose the differential imaginary part of the dielectric function into classes defined by multi-photon resonances.
model_or_system: The system is pumped Germanium, treated as a gapped semiconductor. The analysis involves modeling photo-excited electrons and holes across different momentum states ($k$-points) in the Brillouin zone.
key_observables: Transient absorptive response ($\delta\Im{\epsilon}(\omega, t_{	ext{pr}})$), residual electronic population ($N_{	ext{res}}$), and the phase of oscillatory components (e.g., $2\omega_{	ext{pu}}$).
important_parameters: Pump pulse parameters include $	au_{	ext{pu}} = 13.3 	ext{ fs}$ and $\hbar\omega_{	ext{pu}} = 1.55 	ext{ eV}$. A numerical threshold of $2 	imes 10^{-6}$ is used to define resonant k-points.
main_assumptions: The analysis separates contributions tied to real charge excitation distribution from those associated with virtual processes, although the distinction itself is a focus of investigation.
figures_summary: Figures compare $\delta\Im{\epsilon}(\omega, t_{	ext{pr}})$ calculated using different subsets of k-points (off-resonant vs. resonant) and show momentum-resolved decomposition by resonance class, alongside time delay analysis for the $2\omega_{	ext{pu}}$ component.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need to resolve momentum contributions, develops a theoretical framework based on DPOA/linear response theory, calculates the differential dielectric function using resonance classes (1-, 2-, 3-photon), and finally interprets the mismatch between real-charge dynamics and the full optical signal.
why_interesting: This work provides a sophisticated methodology for dissecting complex many-body responses in solids by mapping physical observables onto specific, quantized momentum-space resonances, which is highly relevant to understanding non-equilibrium quantum dynamics.
